analysis.investment_thesis: Go Digit is an insurance company — a category I explicitly exclude from the Magic Formula because insurance balance sheets distort every metric I rely on. Even forcing the calculation, an earnings yield of ~1.7% (EBIT ₹494 Cr / EV ~₹29,894 Cr) and ROCE of 10.8% fail both Magic Formula screens badly.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 44% over 4 years (₹2,252 Cr → ₹9,716 Cr) shows powerful premium growth in a large underpenetrated market
Near-zero debt (D/E 0.07) and strong promoter holding (73%) reduce capital risk
OCF has been positive all 5 years, reflecting consistent premium collection ahead of claims
key_risks: Magic Formula explicitly excludes financial/insurance companies — metrics are structurally incomparable to industrial businesses
EBIT has been negative in 3 of the last 5 years (-114, -283, -269) — profitability is shallow and untested across a full cycle
Valuation is punishing: P/E 58x, EV/EBITDA 44.7x, P/B 6.3x — you are paying a very steep price for early-stage profitability
red_flags: Financial company: excluded from Magic Formula by design — EBIT/EV and ROIC are not meaningful here
Earnings yield of ~1.7% (EBIT ₹494 Cr / EV ₹29,894 Cr) is far below the 6% floor I require
ROIC/ROCE of 10.8% is below the 20% minimum threshold — no moat evidence in the numbers yet
Operating income swings wildly: -₹283 Cr → +₹50 Cr → -₹269 Cr → +₹494 Cr — no earnings predictability
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Go Digit is an insurance company, full stop. My Magic Formula was built for businesses where EBIT/Enterprise Value and EBIT/(Net Working Capital + Net Fixed Assets) are economically meaningful. For an insurer, premiums, float, combined ratios, and loss development reserves govern economics — not capital turns on fixed and working assets. Applying my formula here would be like measuring a bank's inventory turns. Even if I force the math: EV ≈ ₹29,894 Cr against 2025 EBIT of ₹494 Cr gives an earnings yield of just 1.7%. ROCE is 10.8%. Both are disqualifying — I want >12% earnings yield and >20% ROIC simultaneously.

The business story is genuinely interesting: 44% revenue CAGR, digital-first distribution, near-zero leverage, and the company finally crossed into sustained profitability in FY2025 (₹425 Cr net profit). But profitability was negative in 3 of the last 5 years, the combined ratio environment has been volatile, and the market is pricing this at 58x trailing earnings and 6.3x book. There is no margin of safety. A growth-focused investor with expertise in insurance economics might find this worth watching at a much lower price, but it is firmly outside my circle of competence and my formula.
